questions.q: What is the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution, and why is it given this name?
questions.a: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is called the heart and soul. It is named this because it gives citizens the power to go to court if their rights are violated, making the entire Constitution "alive" and effective. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the Constitution is just a list of suggestions rather than a binding legal document.

questions.q: If a person is arrested by the police but is never told the reason why, what can they do according to our Constitution?
questions.a: They can approach the court to seek justice, as the law requires reasons to be provided for an arrest. A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding that Fundamental Rights are only for the government to follow if they choose, rather than being mandatory.

questions.q: If a shopkeeper refuses to sell you something only because of your caste, which part of the legal system can you use to protect your right?
questions.a: You can approach the court. First, identify that this is discrimination, then recognize that the court is the authority that enforces your right to equality. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks they must personally fight the shopkeeper or accept the discrimination.

questions.q: How does the existence of courts change the way we look at Fundamental Rights compared to a "promise" made by a friend?
questions.a: A promise from a friend is voluntary, but a Fundamental Right is legally binding; courts can force the law to be followed. A wrong answer shows the student does not yet grasp that Fundamental Rights have the power of the State behind them.

questions.q: Should a citizen be able to go to court even if the person violating their right is a powerful government official?
questions.a: Yes, because the Constitution is supreme, and Fundamental Rights apply equally to everyone, including officials. A wrong answer indicates a misunderstanding that "law" applies only to common people and not those in power.

questions.q: Create a short story about a situation where someone’s freedom of speech is stopped. How would they use the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
questions.a: A good story would show a person being silenced for expressing an opinion, followed by them or a representative taking the matter to a court to challenge the restriction. A poor answer fails to show the court process as the solution, perhaps suggesting violence or silence as the response.
